source: Confluence 3160113208 — [Settings] Configurable payment application engine (FDD), SD-16243 Iteration 1
note: No Figma frames exist for this feature yet; this is a text spec extract. Judge fidelity against these normative statements only.
scope_of_iteration_1: Requires 'Apply payments to invoices' to be on
New UI reached by a button in GSP integration settings that opens an OVERLAY (not a toggle in the old Default form)

normative_rules.rule: Override, no fallback: while the engine is on, the default matcher never runs for that integration at any point. If the engine selects nothing the outcome is the Outcome rules, never default behaviour.

Three scope rows only — Customer (CustomerRef), Invoice date (TxnDate >= payment date − N AND TxnDate <= payment date + N, symmetric), Invoice-number match (DocNumber <op> value from a selectable source). Each enabled row contributes one AND clause. There is no locked Open-invoices-only / Balance > 0 row.
The scope query carries an explicit sort: TxnDate ASC, Id ASC.

The invoice-number scope row offers ONLY the four operands QBO accepts in a query: is equal to, contains, starts with, ends with. Default is 'is equal to'. The six negation/empty operands must NOT appear on that row.
The condition box offers all ten operands (the four above plus does not contain, is not equal to, does not start with, does not end with, is empty, is not empty).
The invoice-number scope row's target is always DocNumber. Condition rows may target DocNumber (Invoice number) or PrivateNote (Memo on statement).
Selectable source fields: Invoice number, Invoice note, Invoice id, Subscription id, Invoice metadata (needs a key), Payment note, Payment metadata (needs a key).

Scope validity guard: of Customer and Invoice-number match, at most one may be disabled. Both off is not saveable, blocked with exactly: 'Keep either Customer or the invoice-number match on — otherwise Synder has to look at every invoice in your books.'

Customer inheritance ('a payment that matches an invoice takes its customer from that invoice') is available AND REQUIRED only when the Customer scope row is off. Saving with Customer off and inheritance off must be blocked.
Metadata source with no key entered: save blocked with 'Enter the metadata key to match on.'

Invoice date OFF means no date limit and is admin-enabled only. There is no separate no-limit control. When the org is not admin-enabled the off-switch is disabled. When it is, turning it off is allowed and the UI must disclose that this means no date limit. Finite N while the row is on is self-serve.
One condition box with one AND/OR for the whole box. Row order is not a combinator. Several boxes are not offered in Iteration 1.

Comparison semantics: case-insensitive everywhere; both sides trimmed; DocNumber holds at most 21 characters and the same truncation is applied to the comparison value before testing; the character limit and truncation must be stated on the field.
Absent vs empty: absent (type has no such field, or null, or a missing metadata key) means the row is SKIPPED as not applicable. Empty ('') is a value and operands evaluate normally.
Outcome — condition box selected an invoice: apply the payment to it, then the overpayment rule if the amount exceeds the due.
Outcome — EMPTY box (zero configured rows) with a non-empty snapshot: apply to the FIRST invoice in snapshot order (scope-only).

Outcome — empty snapshot, OR all configured rows not applicable, OR the box had applicable rows and no invoice satisfied it: process as usual as no open invoice was found. Must NOT apply to the first invoice in the snapshot in these cases.
'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' is ONE stored value shown on both the overlay and GSP; either surface can change it and the other inherits. Not a second copy.

'Apply as overpayment' defaults to ON and is a distinct setting from cancel-on-no-match: it fires only after an invoice was matched and the payment amount exceeds that invoice's due. Off means cancel the sync instead.
S1.1: on first open the engine is off, the default matching behaviour is displayed as NON-EDITABLE reference information, and no configuration is pre-filled.
S1.5: switching the engine off returns that integration to the default matcher AND retains the configuration, so re-enabling does not require rebuilding it.
S1.3: below Pro the setting is not configurable and the plan requirement is stated.
S1.4: with 'Apply payments to invoices' off the engine is inert, and the overlay states that payments are not being applied to invoices at all.
S3.5 / Q4: when Generic customer is enabled the Customer scope row no longer narrows meaningfully, and this must be surfaced at configuration time.
The configuration page carries an 'In plain terms' disclosure explaining the flow. It is on the config page, not per payment.
Snapshot order is the tie-break ONLY when several invoices satisfy the box.
The feature 'should have a marketable name'. The FDD does not supply one.
